title: The poison cup
hookLine: legend says poison sent to Mira turned to nectar
tomorrow: poison failed. so what did Mira do when told to stop dancing?

cards: Theo's dad texted him last night, and Theo forwarded it to Zoe: glad you brought your spiritual friend; maybe she can help you find a real church. Zoe has typed three replies and deleted all three.
The palace of Mewar sent Mira something too. The legend says the Rana, the ruler of her husband's family, had a cup prepared and sent to her as an offering for Krishna. Inside was poison.

teach.b: Mira takes the cup, but she doesn't drink right away. She sets it before Krishna, offers it to him, and then drinks.
In the stories it does her no harm; the poison has become amrit, nectar. A song in her name tells it with a laugh: the Rana sent a cup of poison, and Mira drank it laughing.
Here's the teaching under the legend, and it's how offering works at a Krishna shrine: what's offered to God first comes back as his.

The water that has washed the feet of Krishna's image is sipped as a blessing, charanamrit, foot-nectar. Food set before the image comes back as prasad. Mira did the same with a cup meant to kill her.
She offered it, and received it as his. So for the text on Zoe's phone, Mira's cup suggests a third way: not a clapback, not a block. Hold it first, then answer, if she answers at all.
Now two weeks, back around. The weaver, beside you, the swing, none worse than me, the moon inside, only flowers, in the granth, mocking the empty.
Then Lalla's two cloths, from without to within, in my own house, two names. Mira.

how: At Krishna temples and home shrines, charanamrit, water that has bathed the deity's image, is given in small sips as a blessing, and food offered to the deity is shared as prasad; Mira's poison-cup song is sung as a bhajan.

o: the poison Mira offered to Krishna, then drank as nectar
a cup of wine shared at a Rajput royal wedding
a cup of medicine Mira made for the sick

games.q: the cup and the shrine: tap the pairs.
p: sent Mira a cup of poison
offered food that comes back as grace

s: in the legend, Mira refused the cup and fled the palace
she offered it to Krishna first, then drank it, and it did her no harm.
in bhakti, what's offered to God first comes back as his blessing
that's charanamrit and prasad, and it's what Mira did with the cup.
Mira sent a cup of poison back to the palace
she didn't send poison back. a song in her name says she drank it laughing.

games.q: a coworker leaves a nasty note on your desk. you're writing a sharp reply. what would Mira's cup suggest?
o: send the reply now, while it's still sharp
hold it first, offer it up, then answer if at all
tape the note to the break-room wall
games.why: Mira set the cup before Krishna before she drank. offering first changed what came back.

practice: If there's something sweet nearby, a spoon of honey, a piece of fruit, hold it and smell it first. Taste it slowly and let it sit on your tongue.
If there's nothing sweet, take one sip of water as if it were nectar, and let the rest of the time be quiet.

wordCard.voice: The poison cup: the legend of the cup the palace sent Mira, offered to Krishna first and drunk as nectar.

orig.note: Sanskrit and Hindi: nectar, the drink of the gods; in the legend, what the poison became.

carryVoice: Your line: nectar. What's offered first comes back changed. Two weeks of poets, all yours now.
